chapter: Later views and life in Dallas
title: Learning to repair car engines
summary: Smith learned motor repair by watching a friend and now fixes engines for friends at whatever they pay.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Tell me. How did you get into fixing up cars? How did you learn to do that?

I had a friend, worked on my old car all the time. And I always liked that kind of work. He had been doing it for forty years. He passed now, God bless the dead. I told him, I'd like to learn it." He said, "Stay around me." And I had him working on my old car, and he was working on other people's cars, so I just watched him. Then I got pretty good on it, so he said, "Well, you come on and help me, and I'll pay you. Help me fix the motors, tie it down or something or other like that."
But don't you need all kinds of fancy equipment?
Buster Smith - 230
Yeah.
Have you got that?
Yeah. I got nearly everything.
Can you fix transmissions and that kind of thing?
No. I don't fool with transmissions. No, you got to learn something before you can try to do that. They study nothing but that transmission.
So what kind of work do you find you're normally doing on cars?
Motors. I know all of the motor. I know all of the motor, tear it down, put it back together..
Do you have places where you can get spare parts from and that kind of thing?
Mmm-hmm. Yeah.
What about delivery and all that kind of stuff? Do you have to go pick it up?
Yeah, I've got to go pick it up.
Do you make much money at this?

No. I mostly just do it just for livelihood, and I don't go out for it to make really good... I run up on a friend or something or other, and they're having... Like this fellow here, who's sick over there, he's paralyzed. He's got a Buick, kind of a (?) Buick, but he let me fix his car. Just mostly friends and things like that.
Buster Smith - 231
One person leads you to another.
Yeah. They give me something there. They say, 'What do we owe?' I say, 'Give me what you want to give me. Anything you think worthwhile.'
